Strength of association between any two variables

Source: R/association.R
association.Rd

Dependence is measured with the index suited to each pair of variable types (Zuccolotto & Manisera, 2020, Section 3.1): Cramer's V for two categorical variables, the correlation ratio eta-squared for a categorical and a numerical one, and Pearson's correlation for two numerical ones. association() does all three for every pair in vars and puts them on one 0-1 scale (|r| for two numerical variables), with a test p-value, so they can be read in one table or one heatmap (plot_association()).

Usage

association(data, vars)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

vars

Columns to use; a named vector sets display names.

Value

A tibble with var1, var2, measure ("V", "eta2" or "|r|"), value and p_value.

Details

Logical columns and character columns are treated as categorical. With large data almost everything is "significant"; read the strength, not the p-value.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sh <- shots_2024[sample(nrow(shots_2024), 5000), ]
sh$dist <- sqrt(sh$x^2 + sh$y^2)
association(sh, c("league", "value", "made", "dist"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   var1   var2  measure      value  p_value
#>   <chr>  <chr> <chr>        <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 league value V       0.00537    7.04e- 1
#> 2 league made  V       0.0183     1.95e- 1
#> 3 league dist  eta2    0.00000650 8.57e- 1
#> 4 value  made  V       0.186      1.10e-39
#> 5 value  dist  eta2    0.817      0       
#> 6 made   dist  eta2    0.0568     1.74e-65
